Laboratory tests: Blood workup showed mild leukocytosis (18.5 × 109/L). Urine analysis was negative. Pus culture isolated P. aeruginosa, susceptible to ceftazidime and ofloxacin.
Imaging studies:  1. Doppler ultrasonography: Revealed an enlarged left testis with heterogeneous echo pattern, enhanced vascularity, and retained testicular blood flow.

records.query: Need serum tumor markers (AFP, hCG) and CRP to complete the infectious workup and definitively exclude testicular tumor, as the heterogeneous echo pattern on Doppler can mimic malignancy; also need contrast-enhanced scrotal ultrasound or MRI to assess for abscess formation and guide management.

bindings.label: Left scrotal soreness and oedema for five days
Patient is a 13-year-old boy with no lower urinary tract symptoms and no major relevant medical or surgical history
Based on penile characteristics, the patient was diagnosed with occult penis; other congenital anomalies of the genitourinary tract were excluded based on imaging findings

Physical examination revealed an enlarged testis, epididymis, and infected appendages; no torsion was evident in the sperm vessels, but purulent foci were visible on the surface of the vessels with a tough and inseparable texture; the patient was at Tanner stage G4P4
Laboratory tests show leukocytosis and pus culture grows Pseudomonas aeruginosa
Doppler ultrasound shows enlarged left testis with heterogeneous echo, enhanced vascularity, and preserved blood flow
Urinalysis is negative for lower urinary tract infection
Follow-up Doppler ultrasound reveals a mild whirlpool sign
